newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs need bounce to 136.42 for strength.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs need bounce to 136.42 for strength.

text.p: LIFFE September BTP futures will remain negative but need to retrace higher to gather strength, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
"BTPs have fallen quite aggressively. Now we are going to have to move back above 136.42 for some strength to come into the market," said Susan Rigg, technical analyst at Chart Analysis in London.
"We have had a good rally since April which makes a correction not surprising, but the speed with which we are coming down makes a bounce likely sooner or later."
At 0827 GMT, September BTP futures were at 135.19, up 0.04.
But Rigg said the market might not see a move higher just yet.
David Wood, independent technical analyst near London, agreed a bounce up was needed, saying that if BTPs could regain 135.55 and put in a base there, they could then project higher.
"It is becoming difficult to sell because it has come so far without any real retracements," he said.
"But things look very soft across the board so it is hard to see what is going to give BTPs support at the moment."
Wood said the contract had taken out a good support level at 135.35 and would continue to look weak while below 135.15.
He said immediate support was offered by a band from 134.85 to 134.70.
"The implications of a break of 134.70 are a 100 basis point fall to 133.75 which seems a bit unlikely," he said.
Rigg said the market could expect some support to come in around 133.50, the end of June trading range.
"But it will be minor and limited," she said.
At the short end, September Eurolira futures were at 93.20, unchanged on the day.
